headline: Asterloom revisiting price with finance: prepaid-vs-credit surprise and a quote that rose from INR 26,000 to 39,000

suggested_routes.label: Deal / partner next step
suggested_routes.rationale: A returning prospect, with a finance stakeholder present, wants a proposal; the CFO approves; a pilot of 4–5 employees.
suggested_routes.output: Proposal (Team member A: "I will send the cards proposal", turn 35). Itemise recurring INR 26,000 + tax and one-time INR 13,000 integration separately (turns 22–24). Address the setup charge the customer asked to make attractive (turn 25). Scope a 4–5 employee pilot (turn 26) and state that card review is included without the reimbursement module (turn 32). The customer wants details first and will decide internally with the CFO before another call (turns 28, 36).

suggested_routes.label: Sales coaching
suggested_routes.rationale: The price surprise and the prepaid-vs-credit surprise both came from expectations not set earlier.
suggested_routes.output: Coaching note: (1) quote recurring and one-time charges separately from the first conversation. The customer heard INR 26,000 before and INR 39,000 now (turn 23), which damages trust in a deal that has "been discussing this for a long time" (turn 25). (2) Say early that domestic cards are prepaid; the buyer expected a corporate credit card (turn 6). (3) Don't promise unbuilt functionality casually: automatic sync after approval was described as "something we can build" (turn 16).

suggested_routes.label: Internal / product / vendor note
suggested_routes.rationale: Product signal: credit demand and auto-sync-after-approval appear as gaps.
suggested_routes.output: Product note: the buyer expected credit, not prepaid (turn 6), the same theme as Cedarwave (M04 turn 11). Automatic accounting sync after approval is not available today (turn 16). The buyer needs to tell recorded spending apart from spending whose review is complete (turn 17).

evidence.quote: My finance colleague is joining today because we need to understand how this would actually work, and then revisit the price.
Wait, these are prepaid? I had thought about a corporate credit card.
If you need automatic syncing after approval, that is something we can build.
But you previously told me INR 26,000. Why has that become INR 39,000?
evidence.supports: Price inconsistency noticed by the buyer.

evidence.quote: INR 26,000 plus tax is the recurring annual subscription, and INR 13,000 is the one-time accounting integration setup.
We have been discussing this for a long time and still need to decide whether it is the right tool.
but would start with perhaps four or five employees.
Our CFO approves the larger payments.
Send the details first. We need time with the CFO and will tell you if another call is needed.

concise_output: Asterloom returned with a finance colleague to understand the card workflow and revisit price. Two surprises came up mid-meeting: the cards are prepaid, not credit, and the quote rose from INR 26,000 to 39,000 because setup was bundled in. They want a written proposal and will decide with their CFO before scheduling more.
what_established: Use case: domestic travel and small operating expenses; a pilot of 4–5 employees; CFO approval required; recurring INR 26,000 + tax and one-time INR 13,000 setup; the customer wants the proposal made attractive, including setup.
what_not_established: A purchase commitment, timing, or deal value. Spend estimates (INR 10–13 lakh/month; vendor payments INR 26–39 lakh) are explicitly unverified ("that needs checking"). Whether a second meeting will happen.
next_action: Send an itemised proposal scoped to the pilot; brief the rep on expectation-setting.
uncertainty: Speaker-to-organiser mapping is not supplied. All amounts are as spoken in adapted text.
